title: Weave Router beats every router Vals tested on Terminal-Bench 4.0
summary: Weave Router solved 54.5% of Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks on the first attempt. The best of six routers on the Vals Router Index solved 46.5%. Scores, cost per solved task and method.
body_markdown:
Two things stand out.


- **Weave Router is the only router above the best Vals score.** Every other router sits at or below 46.5%.
- **Weave Router has the lowest cost per solved task.** It costs $2.22 for each task it solves on the first attempt. The next router, Nexus Auto with Sol from Fireworks, costs $2.52.


Cost per solved task is cost per trial divided by Pass@1. We derived it from the published numbers. Neither Vals nor Weave reports it directly.


## Beats Fireworks, OpenRouter, Ramp and Sakana on score and cost per solve


Weave Router solved more tasks than all six routers, and cost less for each task it solved:

Weave Router solved 54.5% of tasks at $2.22 per solved task.


## Frontier-model results at about half the cost


Vals found that none of the six routers it tested sits on the cost and accuracy frontier: a single model beat each one on both score and cost. Weave Router is the only router in these comparisons that delivers frontier-model results at about half the cost.


In Weave's paired launch evaluation, with the same Codex harness, the same 66 Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks, the same day and the same package, Weave Router solved 62.1% of tasks against 60.6% for GPT-6 Astra, a frontier single model. It cost $5.22 per trial against $10.03, 52% of the cost, and ran 2.2x faster.


Against OpenRouter's Auto router on the same tasks and graders, Weave Router solved 62.1% against 25.0%, 37.1 points higher, at $5.22 against $5.52 per trial. That Auto run used an earlier policy that OpenRouter has since replaced.


These are pass@2 results from the September launch run, not first-attempt scores, so they aren't directly comparable with the Pass@1 figures above. The full tables, including SWE-Atlas, are in the[Router 2.0 launch post](https://weaveos.com/blog/introducing-weave-router-2-0) .


## How this was measured


**Terminal-Bench 4.0** is 66 terminal tasks, each checked by its own tests. **Pass@1** is the share of tasks solved on the first attempt.


- **Weave Router** was run by Weave on all 66 tasks, two attempts each, in November 2026, through two harnesses. With Claude Code it solved 54.5% of tasks at $5.31 per trial. With Codex it solved 42.4% at $0.94 per trial, which is $2.22 per solved task. The Pass@1 above is the Claude Code run, and the cost per solved task is the Codex run. Cost per trial is the list price of the models the router served.
- **The other six routers'** scores and costs are what Vals AI published on November 3, 2026, at each router's default settings.


The runs were done separately, so treat a gap of a few points as a tie. The 95% intervals for the top four routers overlap. Weave Router's lead is the higher score on this task set, not a statistically proven gap. Vals has not run Weave Router.


These are first-attempt scores. Weave Router's[launch benchmarks](https://weaveos.com/blog/introducing-weave-router-2-0) report pass@2 on a separate September run, so the two sets of numbers aren't directly comparable.


## Try it on your own work


Benchmarks describe one task set. The test that matters is your own agent sessions. Weave Router works with the Claude Code and Codex clients you already use.[Set up Weave Router](https://weaveos.com/router/quickstart) , or[reproduce the benchmark](https://github.com/weave-os/router/tree/main/bench) with the public harness.
